doi_repair.basis: Round-2 recovery high confidence: CrossRef search for 'epigallocatechin gallate trapping deoxyosone xylose alanine Maillard' surfaced the SI record 10.1021/acs.jafc.0c00200.s001; the parent record and the PubMed abstract (PMID 31957424) confirm both of the repo's numeric anchors exactly: EGCG lowers the activation energy for xylose/alanine -> ARP conversion 'from 77.8 to 62.8 kJ/mol' (= 15.0 kJ/mol reduction) and improves the ARP (N-(1-deoxy-D-xylulos-1-yl)alanine) yield 'from 2 to 95%'. off_note_reference_anchors.value_provenance_note: 2026-08-27 (Wave I, cold-start red-team finding): this value is NOT an independently measured concentration in this repo's chain of custody. The arithmetic is exact: OAV 280 (the value the intake registry records for this anchor, 'Defined raw-pea hexanal baseline: 1260 ug/kg (OAV ~280)') x 4.5 ppb, where 4.5 ppb is THIS REPO'S OWN hexanal odour-detection threshold -- itself a compilation-level number that has never been read off a primary table (see the hexanal ODT anchor's harmonization_note in this file; published aqueous hexanal ODTs span 0.3-14 ug/L). 280 x 4.5 = 1260.0 to the digit. It is therefore possible that the source reports 1260 ug/kg directly and the OAV is the derived quantity -- but that has NOT been confirmed against the paper, and the exact divisibility by our own unsourced constant is precisely why the two readings cannot be told apart from inside the repo. Scored as a hold-out point it is a consistency check against our own threshold, not an external measurement, and it MOVES if that threshold is ever corrected.

doi_repair_reversal.how_it_surfaced: Wave I regenerated the hold-out bundles (which had not been regenerated since the sweep). The regeneration rewrote the benchmark's source_doi from 9b07711 to 0c00200 and deleted the citation_audit_note that contradicted it. The stale artifact had been masking a live data defect.

source_status_repair.basis: The current DOI is definitively wrong: 10.1021/jf00111a008 is Purcell & Walter (1982), 'Stability of amino acids during cooking and processing of sweet potatoes'. The work actually meant by 'Grosch (1982)' in the lipid-oxidation literature is the Elsevier book chapter above - it is a real, widely-cited chapter (CrossRef indexes only a 1982 Food Chemistry review OF the book, 10.1016/0308-8146(82)90085-1, not the chapter itself), and it carries no DOI. It is also not a JAFC paper as the repo backlog claims. | I could NOT confirm that the specific value hexanal ODT = 4.5 ppb appears in Grosch (1982). Published hexanal odour thresholds in water span 0.3-14 ug/L across studies, so 4.5 ppb is in range but unattributed. The nearest verifiable primary source for hexanal thresholds from Grosch's own group is Ullrich & Grosch (1987), 'Identification of the most intense volatile flavour compounds formed during autoxidation of linoleic acid', Z. Lebensm. Unters. Forsch. 184:277-282, DOI 10.1007/BF01027663 - but I could not read its threshold table (Springer paywall), so I do not assert it contains 4.5 ppb. Treat the hexanal ODT as unsourced until the value is read off a table.
